title: introduce-session-proxy-and-unify-retry-presets-across-py-ts-go-sdks
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Updates ergonomic session proxy and consolidates retry presets across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs; minor streaming API parity fixes and version bumps for each SDK.
description:
Context and motivation: We continue to see integration friction when customers attempt to use session/lease semantics across product SDKs. Different names (SessionFacade vs SessionProxy vs SessionHandle), subtle differences in retry defaults, and streaming resume hooks cause support churn (SUP-342) and subtle regressions in production integration tests. This PR introduces a minimal, ergonomic SessionProxy abstraction and aligns the default retry profiles for auth and streaming across the three SDKs so teams can rely on consistent behavior across language boundaries.

What this PR changes (high-level):
- Introduces SessionProxy (language-specific implementations) as a lightweight, well-documented facade around credential refresh + heartbeat + optional lease semantics. The goal is parity in surface and predictable lifecycle but with language-idiomatic ergonomics.
- Unifies retry presets: auth window, reauth backoff and circuit-fail fast profiles now live in a single cross-sdk spec under /docs/retry-presets.md and have been wired into each SDK.
- Streaming ergonomics: standardizes resume-token handling and exposes a pullstream-friendly cancel hook. TypeScript and Python expose async iterators with a resume(token) helper; Go exposes a StreamCursor with Resume(token) to match semantics.
- Minor parity fixes: bugfixes to Python's token rotation path when a streaming resume occurs mid-KV-cache restore; TypeScript fix for backpressure hint propagation; Go fixes around session shutdown ordering.
- Version bumps: python 1.15.0, typescript 2.9.0, go 1.6.3 (packaged in SDK meta manifests).

Files touched (representative list):
- redwood-sdk-python/src/session_proxy.py (new)
- redwood-sdk-python/tests/test_session_proxy.py (new)
- redwood-sdk-typescript/src/sessionProxy/index.ts (new)
- redwood-sdk-typescript/src/streaming/resume.ts (fix)
- redwood-sdk-go/sessionproxy/proxy.go (new)
- redwood-sdk-go/streaming/stream_cursor.go (fix)
- docs/retry-presets.md (new cross-sdk spec)
- packages/meta/versions.json (updated)

Commits (summary):
- 7a3f2b1: add SessionProxy shim to python SDK, initial tests and docs
- 9c2d4ef: add SessionProxy implementation to TS SDK, wire resume helper and backpressure hinting
- b4d1c8a: add Go sessionproxy package and StreamCursor Resume semantics
- d0f8b77: extract retry preset spec and wire into SDKs (py/ts/go)
- e3f9a02: fix flakey test and adjust CI definitions for Python integration test (increase timeout)

Testing and CI:
- Local unit tests added for all three SDKs. Python integration tests were run in a staging cluster to validate session heartbeats and token rotation during stream resume; the original run surfaced a flaky Python streaming test that timed out under qemu-based CI runners. I increased the test timeout and added a targeted retry in the test harness.
- CI summary: build (pass), lint (pass), unit-tests (pass), integration-staging (initial fail on py_stream_test, rerun -> pass). Final CI status: pass.

Review notes and decisions:
- API design trade-offs: SessionProxy intentionally keeps a thin surface: start/stop, lease(), lease_release(), resume(token), and with optional context managers/helpers in Py/TS. We debated exposing lower-level heartbeat knobs but deferred to avoid surface bloat.
- Retry presets: the presets are conservative for safety but include a "balanced" profile used by default. Advanced users can opt into aggressive/low-latency profiles via explicit config.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add SessionProxy implementations for Py/TS/Go
- [x] Add tests (unit + targeted integration)
- [x] Update docs/retry-presets.md and SDK changelogs
- [x] Bump meta package versions
- [x] Get approvals from SDK owners

Follow-ups (future work):
- Add a migration guide for existing customers who used previous session facades (small doc to map old names to SessionProxy).
- Consider small heartbeat tuning experiment to reduce tail latency for low-QPS clients.

Backwards compatibility notes: The change is additive; old APIs remain but are deprecated in TypeScript and Python (deprecation warnings added). Go had no prior facade with identical shape so no breaking change. Deprecation period planned for one release cycle.

Merge outcome: Squash merge to main after final CI green and approvals.

Related items: Linear ENG-2145 (session proxy spec), ENG-2180 (retry preset consolidation), Support SUP-342 (customer impact).
